Author: Alex Chapin
Message:
feat: implement nexus config show subcommand (issue #1237) (#1266)

* feat: implement nexus config show subcommand (issue #1237)

Add 'nexus config show' to dump the resolved effective configuration
as a table with KEY, VALUE, SOURCE (env/file/default), and RELOAD
(hot-reloadable via SIGHUP) columns.

Flags:
  --json        Emit as a JSON object keyed by env var name
  --reloadable  Show only the 15 hot-reloadable knobs
  --diff <file> Compare against a YAML/.env file and show only
                keys that differ from the resolved config

The implementation adds ShowFields() to Config which returns a sorted
[]ConfigField, and wires it into cmd/nexus via runConfigShow().
The 'nexus config' usage text is updated to document the new
subcommand and its flags.

* fix: allowlist internal/config/config.go in gitleaks (generic-api-key false positive)

The nexus config show subcommand adds internal/config/config.go which
contains struct field names like ProxyAPIKey and NEXUS_FRONTIER_API_KEY
env var strings. These trigger the generic-api-key rule (issue #313)
as false positives — no real secrets are present. Add the file to the
path-based allowlist alongside the other config false positives.

Description: Identified a pattern that may indicate AWS credentials, risking unauthorized cloud resource access and data breaches on AWS platforms.
Author: Alex Chapin
Message:
feat: resolve #1172 — configurable PII/secret redaction from upstream responses (#1210)

* feat: resolve #1172 — configurable PII/secret redaction from upstream responses

Add ResponseRedactor http.ResponseWriter wrapper that scans every
Write against configurable regex profiles (secrets, pii, custom) and
replaces matches with [REDACTED] before bytes reach the client.

Profiles:
- secrets: sk-, AKIA, ghp_, xoxb-, AIza, PEM private keys
- pii: credit cards (Luhn-validated), SSNs, email addresses
- custom: operator-supplied comma-separated regexes

Streaming-safe: rolling buffer (default 4 KiB) holds cross-chunk
multi-line patterns (e.g. PEM keys split across SSE events).

Writer chain: upstream -> ResponseRedactor -> captureWriter ->
ObservingWriter -> ResponseWriter. Captured content (judge samples,
debug traces) is also redacted.

New config vars: NEXUS_REDACT_ENABLED, NEXUS_REDACT_PROFILE,
NEXUS_REDACT_PATTERNS, NEXUS_REDACT_BUFFER_BYTES. Disabled by default
so existing deployments are byte-for-byte identical.

New metric: nexus_redacted_total{profile="..."}.

Add buffered batch writes to JSONLRecorder with configurable size
(64 KiB default) and time-based (5s default) flush triggers. A
Sync() method provides immediate flush; Close() performs a final
flush before closing. On write failure, oldest buffered records
are dropped and a rotation is attempted.

- NEXUS_JSONL_BUFFER_SIZE: buffer threshold before flush (default 64 KiB)
- NEXUS_JSONL_FLUSH_INTERVAL: max time between flushes (default 5s)

Implementation:
- Memory buffer ([]byte) accumulates serialized records
- Background goroutine drains the buffer on: size threshold,
  time ticker, explicit Sync() signal, or channel close
- Rotation check updated to account for buffered bytes
- Close-time rotation check handles buffered data correctly
- SQLiteStore and test helpers updated to implement new Sync() method

- Rotation tests (maxBytes small relative to default buffer) now use
  bufferSize=1 to verify per-record flush behavior

Fixes #745 — remove unconditional sortExpiry() call in Set and
SetEmbedding that caused O(n log n) overhead on every insertion
regardless of whether eviction occurred.

sortExpiry() is already called inside evictExpired() when eviction
actually happens. The unconditional calls in Set/SetEmbedding were
redundant for the no-eviction path and harmful for performance.

sortExpiry() after Unlock() in the previous implementation created
a window where concurrent evictExpired (holding the write lock and
sorting expiry) could race with the post-Unlock sort call.

* fix: resolve flaky TestNewVRAMLimiterContextCancelReleasesBlocked

The test expected DeadlineExceeded from context.WithTimeout + time.Sleep(50ms),
but on loaded CI runners the 50ms window is insufficient to guarantee the waiter
goroutine has entered cond.Wait() before cancel() fires. When cancel() fires first
(via the timeout or explicitly), ctx.Err() is Canceled, not DeadlineExceeded.

Fix: accept Canceled OR DeadlineExceeded (both valid cancel errors), and increase
the sleep to 500ms to ensure the waiter is parked on fast machines.

Ref: TestAcquireContextCancelPreWaitRace already uses Canceled for the same
scenario and is the correct error for context cancellation paths.

* feat: add embed circuit breaker to SLMCache (issue #982)

When the embedder returns errors on Set, track recent failure timestamps
in a 3-entry circular buffer. If 3 failures occur within 30 seconds,
skip calling the embedder for the next 30s to avoid a retry loop against
a consistently failing embedder.

Adds embedBreaker [3]time.Time, embedBreakerPos int, and
embedCooldownUntil time.Time fields to SLMCache. Adds constants
embedFailureCooldownThreshold (3) and embedFailureCooldownWindow (30s).

The fix uses modulo arithmetic for safe circular buffer writes:
  writeIdx := c.embedBreakerPos % embedFailureCooldownThreshold

Cooldown expiration is checked via time.Now().Before(embedCooldownUntil),
skipping the embed call when the cooldown is active.

* fix: make TestMiddleware_Reaper_Once deterministic with WaitGroup

The test previously relied on time.Sleep(100ms) to wait for the reaper
goroutine to exit after Stop(), which is unreliable under the race detector
in CI. Add a sync.WaitGroup to the Middleware struct so Stop() blocks
until the reaper has fully exited, making the goroutine-count assertion
deterministic.

This also fixes the Stop() method to be blocking, which is the standard
Go pattern (e.g., http.Server.Shutdown).
